mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines over the prior month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) and elevated interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) signal a stagflationary environment that triggers equity sell-offs, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where both CPIAUCSL > 3.5 and FEDFUNDS > 4.5, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime characterized by low unemployment (UNRATE < 3.5%) and strong labor market growth (PAYEMS monthly change > 50), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to overheating concerns, yielding negative 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods meeting the trigger condition, or the Rank IC for the joint condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals robust labor market conditions that support corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with PAYEMS growth, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 for two consecutive months, it indicates a contraction in manufacturing output that reduces corporate profitability expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where INDPRO < 100 for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing boom regime with high new home construction (HOUST > 1400) and strong consumer spending (RSAFS > 700000), the S&P 500 experiences positive returns over the next 60 trading days due to elevated economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods meeting the trigger condition, or the Rank IC for the joint condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strong housing starts (HOUST > 1400) and robust industrial production (INDPRO > 102) signal a synchronized demand-supply expansion that boosts corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where both HOUST > 1400 and INDPRO > 102, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.
